WHC

Wage & Health Equity Compass

County edition — 2,286 U.S. counties, real BLS QCEW wages × real CDC PLACES health data
Wages: BLS QCEW 2025 annual averages, private sector, all industries, county totals. Health measures: CDC PLACES 2025 county release, crude prevalence, joined directly on 5-digit county FIPS.
ⓘ All figures are real and joined on exact county FIPS codes (QCEW area_fips = PLACES LocationID). Of 3,275 QCEW counties, 2,286 had complete PLACES health measures and non-suppressed wage data; the remainder were dropped rather than estimated.

How the burden score works
Seven CDC PLACES crude-prevalence measures are pulled per county: diabetes, obesity, high blood pressure, cost-barrier to care, current smoking, poor mental health days, and food insecurity.

Each measure is converted to a percentile rank (0–100) across all 2,286 counties in this dataset, so a measure with naturally higher raw percentages (like obesity) doesn't dominate the score.

The 7 percentile ranks are then averaged into a single 0–100 burden score. A county at 100 ranks at the very top of this dataset across all seven measures combined; a county at 0 ranks at the very bottom.
How tiers are set
Critical: wage below the national county median ($1,021) and burden score ≥ 80.

High: wage below median and burden ≥ 60.

Watch: either signal alone is elevated.
